symptom: All PCs and Server0 cannot reach their default gateways.
topology_note: R1 G0/0/0 connects to Switch0 G0/1 as the only router-on-a-stick trunk; PC0 and PC2 are VLAN 10, PC1 and Server0 are VLAN 20.
show_output: R1# show ip interface brief | GigabitEthernet0/0/0 unassigned YES unset administratively down down
expected_fault: R1 parent trunk interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0 is administratively shut down.

symptom: PC0 and PC2 cannot reach the VLAN 10 default gateway, while the cable is connected.
topology_note: PC0 and PC2 use VLAN 10 access ports on Switch0; R1 G0/0/0.10 is the VLAN 10 gateway.
show_output: Switch0# show interfaces fa0/1 status | Fa0/1 connected 1; Switch0# show vlan brief | Fa0/1 listed under VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10
expected_fault: PC0 access port is assigned to the wrong VLAN.

symptom: Switch0 management interface cannot ping 192.168.99.1 and CDP reports a native VLAN mismatch.
topology_note: R1 G0/0/0.99 uses encapsulation dot1Q 99 native; Switch0 G0/1 is the trunk and VLAN 99 is management.
show_output: Switch0# show interfaces trunk | Gi0/1 native vlan 1; R1# show running-config interface g0/0/0.99 | encapsulation dot1Q 99 native
expected_fault: Native VLAN values differ: Switch0 uses VLAN 1 but R1 uses VLAN 99.

symptom: PC1 and Server0 cannot reach 192.168.20.1, but PC0 can still reach 192.168.10.1.
topology_note: PC1 and Server0 are in VLAN 20; R1 G0/0/0.20 should provide gateway 192.168.20.1/24.
show_output: R1# show ip interface brief | GigabitEthernet0/0/0.20 192.168.200.1 YES manual up up
expected_fault: VLAN 20 router subinterface has the wrong IP address; 192.168.200.1 is configured instead of 192.168.20.1.

symptom: PC1 and Server0 cannot communicate through the router although their VLAN 20 access ports are correct.
topology_note: PC1 and Server0 use VLAN 20 access ports on Switch0; R1 G0/0/0.20 is their router-on-a-stick gateway.
show_output: R1# show running-config interface g0/0/0.20 | interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0.20; no encapsulation dot1Q 20 line present
expected_fault: Router subinterface for VLAN 20 is missing encapsulation dot1Q 20.

symptom: A VLAN 10 PC has a valid IP address but cannot reach its default gateway.
topology_note: PC0 is on VLAN 10 and R1 G0/0/0.10 is correctly configured as 192.168.10.1/24.
show_output: PC0> ipconfig | IP Address 192.168.10.15; Default Gateway 192.168.10.254; R1# show ip interface brief | G0/0/0.10 192.168.10.1 up up
expected_fault: End device default gateway is configured as 192.168.10.254 instead of 192.168.10.1.

symptom: PC0 intermittently loses connectivity and other hosts report an address conflict.
topology_note: PC0 and PC2 are both VLAN 10 endpoints using static IPv4 configuration.
show_output: PC0> ipconfig | IP Address 192.168.10.15; PC2> ipconfig | IP Address 192.168.10.15; Switch0# show mac address-table dynamic vlan 10 | different MAC addresses observed
expected_fault: PC0 and PC2 have duplicate static IPv4 addresses.

symptom: PC2 cannot communicate even with other VLAN 10 PCs; its switch port is disabled.
topology_note: PC2 connects to Switch0 Fa0/2 as a VLAN 10 access port; port security was enabled for the demonstration.
show_output: Switch0# show port-security interface fa0/2 | Security Violation Count 1; Port Status Secure-shutdown; Switch0# show interfaces fa0/2 status | err-disabled
expected_fault: A port-security violation placed PC2's access port in err-disabled state.

symptom: PC0 can ping its gateway but cannot ping PC1 or Server0; PC1 can still initiate traffic to PC0.
topology_note: PC0 and PC2 are VLAN 10; PC1 and Server0 are VLAN 20; ACL is applied inbound on R1 G0/0/0.10.
show_output: R1# show access-lists 110 | deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255; R1# show running-config interface g0/0/0.10 | ip access-group 110 in
expected_fault: Inbound ACL 110 deliberately blocks traffic from VLAN 10 to VLAN 20.

symptom: PC1 receives an address but cannot communicate correctly with VLAN 20 hosts after DHCP configuration.
topology_note: PC1 belongs to VLAN 20; R1 G0/0/0.20 is the gateway at 192.168.20.1/24; DHCP service is provided by Server0 or R1.
show_output: DHCP lease for PC1 | IP Address 192.168.20.25; Subnet Mask 255.255.255.128; expected subnet mask 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: DHCP pool or PC1 configuration supplies the wrong /25 subnet mask instead of /24.

symptom: Server0 is reachable by IP address from PC0 but cannot be reached by hostname.
topology_note: Server0 provides DNS service on VLAN 20; PC0 is a VLAN 10 client and inter-VLAN routing is verified with successful IP ping.
show_output: PC0> ipconfig /all | DNS Server blank; PC0> ping 192.168.20.10 succeeds; PC0> ping server0.lab fails
expected_fault: PC0 has no DNS server configured, despite working Layer 3 connectivity.

symptom: The trunk link has frequent errors and VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 traffic becomes unstable.
topology_note: R1 G0/0/0 connects to Switch0 G0/1 by one Ethernet trunk cable.
show_output: Switch0# show interfaces g0/1 | input errors and CRC errors increasing; log shows line protocol up/down repeatedly
expected_fault: Physical trunk cable or interface has a Layer 1 fault causing errors and link flapping.

symptom: VLAN 10 hosts can communicate with each other but cannot reach their router gateway or VLAN 20 hosts.
topology_note: PC0 and PC2 are VLAN 10 access ports; R1 G0/0/0.10 is the VLAN 10 gateway; Switch0 G0/1 is the only trunk.
show_output: Switch0# show interfaces trunk | Gi0/1 allowed VLANs 20,99; VLAN 10 absent from the allowed VLAN list
expected_fault: VLAN 10 is excluded from the switch trunk allowed-VLAN list.

symptom: PC1 and Server0 communicate locally in VLAN 20 but cannot reach 192.168.20.1 or VLAN 10.
topology_note: PC1 and Server0 are VLAN 20 access ports; R1 G0/0/0.20 is the VLAN 20 gateway; Switch0 G0/1 is the only trunk.
show_output: Switch0# show interfaces trunk | Gi0/1 allowed VLANs 10,99; VLAN 20 absent from the allowed VLAN list
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is excluded from the switch trunk allowed-VLAN list.

symptom: All inter-VLAN traffic fails although switch access ports show the correct VLAN assignments.
topology_note: R1 G0/0/0 should connect to Switch0 G0/1 as an 802.1Q trunk carrying VLAN 10, VLAN 20, and VLAN 99.
show_output: Switch0# show interfaces trunk | no interfaces trunking; Switch0# show running-config interface g0/1 | switchport mode access
expected_fault: The router-to-switch uplink is configured as an access port instead of a trunk.

symptom: PC1 cannot reach its VLAN 20 gateway even though the router interface and switch port are correct.
topology_note: PC1 is connected to a VLAN 20 access port; R1 G0/0/0.20 is configured as 192.168.20.1/24.
show_output: PC1> ipconfig | IP Address 192.168.10.25; Default Gateway 192.168.20.1; Switch0# show vlan brief | PC1 port is in VLAN 20
expected_fault: PC1 has a static IP address from VLAN 10 while connected to VLAN 20.

symptom: Server0 cannot reply to requests from VLAN 10 clients, but PC1 on the same VLAN can reach it.
topology_note: Server0 and PC1 are VLAN 20 hosts; R1 G0/0/0.20 is the gateway at 192.168.20.1.
show_output: Server0> ipconfig | IP Address 192.168.20.10; Default Gateway 192.168.20.254; R1# show ip interface brief | G0/0/0.20 192.168.20.1 up up
expected_fault: Server0 has an incorrect default gateway.

symptom: PC0 has no network connectivity while the router trunk and other VLAN 10 host PC2 work normally.
topology_note: PC0 connects to Switch0 Fa0/1 as a VLAN 10 access port; PC2 is another working VLAN 10 host.
show_output: Switch0# show interfaces fa0/1 status | Fa0/1 disabled 10; Switch0# show running-config interface fa0/1 | shutdown
expected_fault: PC0 switch access port is administratively shut down.

symptom: VLAN 10 clients cannot reach their gateway although their IP settings and access ports are correct.
topology_note: PC0 and PC2 are VLAN 10 endpoints; router-on-a-stick uses R1 G0/0/0.10 as the VLAN 10 gateway.
show_output: R1# show running-config interface g0/0/0.10 | encapsulation dot1Q 1; ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: R1 VLAN 10 gateway subinterface has the wrong 802.1Q VLAN tag.

symptom: PC0 can reach its gateway but cannot reach Server0, while other expected traffic is allowed.
topology_note: PC0 is in VLAN 10; Server0 is in VLAN 20; ACL is applied inbound on R1 G0/0/0.10.
show_output: R1# show access-lists 111 | deny icmp host 192.168.10.15 host 192.168.20.10; permit ip any any; R1# show run interface g0/0/0.10 | ip access-group 111 in
expected_fault: ACL 111 specifically blocks ICMP from PC0 to Server0.

symptom: PC0 can ping Server0 by IP address but cannot resolve its hostname.
topology_note: Server0 provides DNS service at 192.168.20.10 and PC0 has verified inter-VLAN IP connectivity.
show_output: PC0> ipconfig /all | DNS Server 192.168.20.254; PC0> ping 192.168.20.10 succeeds; PC0> ping server0.lab fails
expected_fault: PC0 is configured with the wrong DNS server address.

symptom: Clients can reach Server0 by IP address but all hostname lookups fail.
topology_note: Server0 is intended to provide DNS service on 192.168.20.10; Layer 3 connectivity to it is working.
show_output: Server0 DNS service | Service status Off; PC0> ping 192.168.20.10 succeeds; PC0> ping server0.lab fails
expected_fault: DNS service is disabled on Server0.

symptom: PC0 can ping Server0 but cannot open its web page.
topology_note: Server0 provides an HTTP test service at 192.168.20.10; PC0 has a valid VLAN 10 route to the server.
show_output: Server0 HTTP service | Service status Off; PC0> ping 192.168.20.10 succeeds; browser request to http://192.168.20.10 fails
expected_fault: HTTP service is disabled on Server0.

symptom: PC1 remains without an IP address after requesting DHCP.
topology_note: Server0 is used as the VLAN 20 DHCP server; PC1 is connected to a VLAN 20 access port.
show_output: Server0 DHCP service | Service status Off; PC1> ipconfig | IP Address 0.0.0.0 or 169.254.x.x
expected_fault: DHCP service is disabled on Server0.

symptom: PC1 receives a VLAN 20 address through DHCP but cannot reach its correct gateway.
topology_note: Server0 provides the DHCP pool for VLAN 20; R1 G0/0/0.20 gateway is 192.168.20.1/24.
show_output: Server0 DHCP pool VLAN20 | Default Gateway 192.168.20.254; PC1> ipconfig | Default Gateway 192.168.20.254
expected_fault: The VLAN 20 DHCP pool supplies an incorrect default gateway.

symptom: PC1 receives a DHCP address but cannot communicate on VLAN 20.
topology_note: PC1 is connected to a VLAN 20 access port; Server0 hosts DHCP scopes for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20.
show_output: PC1> ipconfig | IP Address 192.168.10.50; Switch0# show vlan brief | PC1 port is in VLAN 20; R1# show ip interface brief | G0/0/0.20 192.168.20.1 up up
expected_fault: A DHCP pool for the wrong subnet is assigned to a VLAN 20 client.

symptom: Server0 cannot communicate with either PC1 in its VLAN or PC0 across the router.
topology_note: Server0 is connected to a VLAN 20 access port with intended address 192.168.20.10/24.
show_output: Server0> ipconfig | IP Address 192.168.30.10; Subnet Mask 255.255.255.0; Default Gateway 192.168.20.1
expected_fault: Server0 has a static IP address from the wrong subnet.

symptom: Server0 can communicate with some VLAN 20 devices but not all expected VLAN 20 addresses.
topology_note: PC1 and Server0 are in the same VLAN 20 subnet, which should use mask 255.255.255.0.
show_output: Server0> ipconfig | IP Address 192.168.20.10; Subnet Mask 255.255.255.128; expected mask 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: Server0 has a /25 subnet mask instead of the required /24 mask.

symptom: VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 users work, but Switch0 cannot be managed reliably from the router management address.
topology_note: Switch0 management SVI is VLAN 99 at 192.168.99.2; R1 G0/0/0.99 is 192.168.99.1.
show_output: Switch0# show ip interface brief | Vlan99 192.168.99.20 up up; R1# show running-config interface g0/0/0.99 | ip address 192.168.99.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: Switch0 management SVI has the wrong IPv4 address.

symptom: A VLAN 10 PC cannot remotely manage Switch0 at 192.168.99.2, although Switch0 can be reached from VLAN 99.
topology_note: Switch0 management SVI is VLAN 99; PC0 is VLAN 10 and reaches other networks through R1 router-on-a-stick.
show_output: Switch0# show running-config | no ip default-gateway command; Switch0# show ip interface brief | Vlan99 192.168.99.2 up up
expected_fault: Switch0 has no default gateway for replies to management traffic from other VLANs.
